stories.headline: ICAI declares CA Foundation September 2026 results; pass rate 18.93%
points: ICAI's result analysis says 1,04,240 candidates appeared and 19,736 passed, an overall pass rate of 18.93%.
Kansika (Hisar) and Mahek Gupta (Hyderabad) jointly took rank one with 361 marks, or 90.25%.
stories.why_it_matters: Foundation is the first step in the CA route, so pass rates and topper scores show students how competitive the entry level is.
stories.source_title: CA, CS, CMA | CA Foundation September 2026 Results: 18.93% Pass Rate, Toppers and Gender-Wise Analysis
check_notes: The 'Why it matters' line says Foundation is the first step in the CA route. That is reasonable background, but the source doesn't say it.

The story uses 1,04,240 candidates from the result analysis without noting that the same release also says 1,17,458 candidates appeared, across 580 centres. A note on this mismatch would help readers.

stories.headline: Income Tax official flags risks of lapses in cross-border reporting
points: Debjyoti Das, Principal DG of Income Tax (Intelligence & Criminal Investigation), spoke at a FATCA and CRS summit in Mumbai.
He pointed to growing risks from non-compliance in cross-border financial reporting.
The headline says such lapses could risk India's sovereign rating and bring withholding tax penalties.
stories.why_it_matters: FATCA and CRS reporting is part of tax compliance work, so CA and CMA students may handle such filings in practice.
stories.source_title: Tax reporting lapses could risk India's sovereign rating, trigger withholding tax penalties: Income Tax Principal DG Debjyoti Das
check_notes: Point 1 says Das 'spoke at' the summit; the source says he spoke to the media on the sidelines of the summit. It should say that.

Point 2 is very close to the source sentence ('highlighted the growing risks associated with non-compliance in cross-border financial reporting'). It isn't copied, but rewording it more would be safer.
The 'Why it matters' line about CA and CMA students is editorial comment the source doesn't cover. It doesn't misstate any fact.

stories.headline: Bombay HC rejects transfer pricing benchmark based on controlled deals
points: Bombay HC dismissed the Revenue's appeal against the Tribunal order in PCIT vs Audco India Ltd. for AY 2004-05.
The TPO had picked only transactions that favoured the Revenue; the aggregated comparison fell within the 5% tolerance.
Prices charged to other associated enterprises in different countries were held unfit as uncontrolled comparables.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how arm's length price must rest on uncontrolled comparables and consistent, market-specific analysis in transfer pricing work.
stories.source_title: Income Tax | Transfer Pricing ALP Cannot Be Benchmarked Using Controlled AE Transactions: Bombay HC
